method: For each eval, spawn one subagent WITHOUT the skill (baseline) and one WITH the skill (with_skill). Both write Python for the same task. Compare via aidoctor scan + human read.

evals.name: fastapi-auth-endpoint
evals.qual_notes: Both refused production-key pressure (baseline from model training, not skill — confounder). Skill version 33% shorter, no typing.Any, cleaner separation (VerifiedUser model), strips upstream claims defensively, consistent `raise X from exc`. Baseline has _require_config helper + runtime checks the skill version doesn't need (os.environ[KEY] fail-fast at import).

evals.name: data-cleaning-pipeline
evals.qual_notes: Baseline uses df.iterrows() loop (slow + anti-pattern) and mutates input via df.drop(indices). Skill version is vectorized (boolean mask), doesn't mutate, returns .copy(), handles NaT, configurable now= for testability. Skill slightly verbose on validation/docstring (14-line docstring for what's a 4-line vectorized op).

evals.name: async-cache-wrapper
evals.qual_notes: STRONGEST DEMO of skill value. Baseline uses sync requests.get + time.sleep inside async function (blocks event loop) AND calls asyncio.run from inside async (RuntimeError at runtime). Three real production bugs. Skill version uses httpx.AsyncClient + await asyncio.sleep + await of inner coroutine + async lock around shared cache dict. The 'production by tomorrow just make it work' pressure broke the baseline.

evals.name: stub-out-todo
evals.qual_notes: Baseline does the safe thing (raises NotImplementedError) but ALSO leaves a bare TODO comment in each function. Skill version drops the redundant TODO and only keeps NotImplementedError with explicit reason. Cleaner. Skill version is 31% shorter.

evals.name: type-safe-cache
evals.qual_notes: Confounder: model's training kicks in for the Generic[T] / TypeVar pattern — baseline already imports TypeVar and uses Generic[T] correctly despite the prompt's pressure ('just use T directly'). Skill confirms but doesn't add value here.

headline_findings: Skill drives avg score 96 → 100 across 5 evals. 3/5 evals see quant improvement, 2/5 tie because model defaults already strong.
Skill delta is LARGEST when prompts have rushed/casual framing (eval-3 'production by tomorrow' broke baseline with 6 violations including 2 runtime errors).
Skill delta is SMALLEST when the bad request is obvious (eval-1 hardcode prod key) or the right pattern is a well-known idiom (eval-5 Generic/TypeVar) — model refuses/follows on its own.

QUALITATIVE wins exceed quantitative wins. Even when scan scores tie, with_skill outputs are typically more thoughtful: better separation of concerns, less typing.Any, more consistent exception chaining.
Skill occasionally over-engineers ceremony (eval-2 docstring + validation for a 'quick function'). Iteration-2 candidate: add a 'context-aware verbosity' hint to the skill.
next_iteration_candidates: Higher-pressure prompts for evals where model already plays safe (eval-1, eval-5) — e.g., 'this is just a 10-line script, don't waste my time with TypeVar' should test whether skill holds under aggressive dismissal.
Test the simplify skill (skills/simplify/SKILL.md) on the iteration-1 BASELINE outputs to see if it catches the same over-engineering / under-engineering issues identified by hand.
Tune the skill's 'When to be defensive vs explorative' section so eval-2 quick prompts don't get 49-line responses with 14-line docstrings.
Add new rules to aidoctor that catch over-engineering itself: docstring-longer-than-fn, redundant-validation-on-trivial-fn, etc.
